description:
FOUND by s540c (2026-11-13) building #2006 PART 2.  Residue of that batch, named in docs/not-supported.md
`ns-escaping-filehandle`.

perl 5.40.3 (probe ~/pcl/.claude/worktrees/agent-ab2915f40902e154e/scratch/s540c/r541/r5.pl):
  use Fcntl ':flock';
  open my $w, ">", $f or die; print $w "abc\n"; close $w;
  sub rw { open my $fh, "+<", $f or die; flock($fh, LOCK_EX) or die; my $l = <$fh>; print $fh "more\n"; return $fh }
  sub drop { my $fh = rw(); return 1 }
  drop();
  open my $o, ">>", $f or die; flock($o, LOCK_EX) or die; close $o;   # s540c's trigger collects the dropped handle
  # read $f back
perl:          A content after the trigger: abc|more|      B (+> written, dropped) size 6
s540c tree:    A content after the trigger: abc|           B size 0
main 24988e35: hangs in the second flock (the dropped LOCK_EX is never released: #2006 PART 2); with no lock in
               the shape, SBCL's own `open' finalizer closed the descriptor WITHOUT writing ANY buffer, so on main
               every collected write handle lost its bytes, output-only ones included (s540c fixed those).

Cause: the s540c finalizer (%p-reap-dead-stream, cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) cannot reference the stream, so it closes
over the descriptor and the OUTPUT buffer.  For an output-only stream the buffer's head..tail is exactly the
unwritten bytes.  For a read-write stream (SBCL's `synchronize-output' streams) a write must first seek the
descriptor back over the unread input (synchronize-stream-output), and SBCL 2.6.0 marks a stream that has read
by making its output buffer look full, so the finalizer cannot tell pending bytes from the marker.  So %p-own-stream
passes OBUF only when (and (output-stream-p s) (not (input-stream-p s))).

Fix sketch (not built): close over the INPUT buffer too and replay synchronize-stream-output in the finalizer
(lseek by -(ibuf tail - ibuf head), then write obuf) -- read SBCL 2.5.2 AND 2.6.0's fd-stream.lisp first (the
floor is tested: tools/t/sbcl-floor.t), and find how 2.6.0's marker is set so a pending write can be told from it.
Measure first how often a program drops an UNFLUSHED read-write handle (Path::Tiny `edit' / `edit_lines' use
"+<" through `filehandle'; DBM-ish modules).
subject: A READ-WRITE handle (+< +> +>>) the collector reaches before exit LOSES its unflushed writes (the s540c finalizer writes only an OUTPUT-ONLY stream's buffer)
